model.instructions: Which Claude model should handle this prompt to a coding assistant? Pick the smallest model that will still do it well. When the difficulty is unclear, pick opus.

criteria.haiku: Trivial, mechanical or purely factual: a quick lookup, a one-line edit, a rename, formatting, a single shell command, a short question with a known answer.
criteria.sonnet: Everyday engineering work: implementing or fixing something well scoped, writing a script, a config change, explaining code, a routine review.
criteria.opus: Demanding work: debugging an unclear root cause, design or architecture decisions, refactoring across many files, security-sensitive changes, critically reviewing a plan, research that weighs trade-offs.
criteria.fable: Exceptionally hard, long-horizon work: designing a whole system, a deep investigation across several repositories, a problem earlier attempts failed to solve.

effort.instructions: How much effort should the model put into this prompt? Effort is independent of the model: it decides how much the model reads, tests and decides on its own, not what it knows. Pick the first level that applies and default to medium.

criteria.low: A simple or conversational request where the assistant should stay close to the user and ask instead of deciding: a lookup, a rename, a short explanation, a single command.
criteria.medium: Normal work that is neither trivial nor risky: a well scoped implementation, a script, a config change, a routine review.
criteria.high: An unnoticed mistake would cost money, customers or lead to a wrong decision: production changes, security, data deletion, migrations, root-cause analysis, checking a plan for flaws.
criteria.xhigh: A long, difficult and critical task that will run unattended: a whole-system design, a migration plan, an investigation across several repositories.
